title: Readiness Heuristics: Pocket Guide for Launch Operators
content:
Context:
This is a compact, operator-focused heuristics guide for quick pre-launch checks, lightweight KPI tracking, and immediate post-launch actions. Intended for small launch squads (PM + Eng + Ops) who want a fast decision surface during the first 72h. Keep it next to your runbook and dashboard during canary/rollouts.

Purpose / scope:
- Short, practical rules-of-thumb and thresholds (not a full playbook).
- Combine product readiness (latency/quality), infra health (capacity/cost), and human processes (oncall, comms).
- Designed for PLG-to-enterprise launches on Redwood hosted or dedicated lanes.

Quick checklist (pre-flight — 1 hour window):
- Canary target: 5–10% of traffic or 100–500 sessions (whichever triggers earlier).
- Verify model pinned version and fallback policy in route config (rollout.policy: canary -> gradual -> full).
- Verify rate limit bucket and emergency throttle (operator must know how to cut traffic to 20%).
- Alerts enabled: p95 latency, errors (5xx), model-output-quality-drop (eval sentinel), cost burn radar.
- Confirm telemetry tags: deployment_id, canary_id, customer_segment, commit_sha.
- Communication: #launch-ops Slack + 1-page status doc shared; rotate a 15-min check-in for first 2 hours.

Core KPIs to surface (first 72h):
- Latency P50 / P95 / P99 (ms): target P95 <= 750ms for general interactive features; P95 <= 350ms for latency-sensitive flows.
- Error rate (5xx or model runtime errors): target < 0.5% (immediate mitigation if >1%).
- Cost rate ($ / 1k tokens or $ / 1k requests): monitor delta vs baseline; target delta < 30% for minor experiments.
- Throughput / capacity burn (GPU-minutes/hr): ensure baseline reserve + 30% buffer for spikes.
- Quality regression (% failed evals vs baseline on probe set): alarm if >5% relative degradation.
- User-visible failures (support tickets / 1k users): keep below 0.2 for the cohort.

Decision thresholds (action ladder):
- Soft alarm (yellow): p95 > threshold OR error rate 0.5–1% OR cost burn +30–50% -> Hold canary expansion, throttle non-critical traffic, start 15-min cadence.
- Hard alarm (red): p95 > 2x target OR error rate >1% OR regressions >5% -> Rollback to previous model/route, notify ESCALATE, open incident channel.
- Cost-only alarm: if cost / 1k tokens > 4x forecast AND user impact low -> switch to quantized model variant or apply batch-size caps.

Triage quick-questions (to drive the runbook):
- Is the spike cross-region or single-region? If cross-region -> suspect routing; if single-region -> suspect infra/host.
- Is the error rate correlated with a particular model version or dataset shard? Check request metadata (input size, long context).
- Did new caching rules miss prefix matches? Verify prefix/KV cache hits.

Minimal observability queries (copy-paste for dashboards):
- Latency distribution per route: SELECT percentile(lat_ms, [50,95,99]) FROM requests WHERE route = '<route>' AND deployment_id = '<id>'
- Error rate per model: SELECT count_if(status >= 500) / count(*) FROM requests WHERE model = '<model>' and timeslice = 1m
- Cost burn by session: GROUP BY session_id SUM(token_cost) ORDER BY SUM(token_cost) DESC LIMIT 50
- KV cache hit ratio: sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_requests) OVER 1m windows

Canary expansion heuristic (micro steps):
- Start: 5% traffic for 30–60m, check KPIs; if green -> 15% for 30m; if green -> 50% for 60m; then 100%.
- If marginal: hold and run stress probe to 2x expected traffic for 15m.
- Never expand if any hard alarm is present.

Runbook snippets (copy-ready actions):
- To throttle traffic to 20% (operator command): cfg set route.<route>.traffic=0.2 --deployment=<id> --reason='throttle due to p95 spike'
- To rollback to previous model: rollout rollback --route=<route> --to-version=<prev_sha> --notify=oncall@redwood.ai
- To quickly switch to cheaper variant: route set model_variant=<quantized_variant> --scale=auto

Communication templates (status update, 1-line):
- "[T+1h] Canary stable: p95=320ms (target 350), errors=0.2%, burn +12%. Proceeding to 15% expansion at T+30m. — @Marina"
- "[ALERT] p95 2.1x target on route <name>. Throttling to 20%, rollback in progress. Incident channel: #inc-launch-564"

Post-launch 72h tasks (ownerable items):
- T+6h: Product + Eng sync (short notes) — check qualitative feedback, early NPS/CSAT probes (owner: PM).
- T+12h: Cost variance report vs forecast (owner: Finance-ops).
- T+24h: Autoscaling profile tuning if sustained >70% capacity (owner: infra eng).
- T+72h: Retro + action items and a change-to-prod decision for full rollout (owner: release lead).

Known tradeoffs and heuristics (explicit):
- Latency vs cost: raising batch windows reduces cost but increases p95. On interactive flows, prefer latency SLOs over marginal cost savings.
- Quantization fallback: use for short-term cost control but validate quality on the probe set (run evals on 1000 requests).
- Aggressive caching: good for repeated prefixes, but watch memory + stale semantics for session-sensitive features.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add a tiny notebook that projects cost delta vs expansion steps (CSV -> graph).
- Create a one-click toggle in console for switching to quantized model variants. Tracking ticket: JIRA-7890.
- Capture sample bad-model-outputs and attach to incident thread for ML debugging.

Appendix: Quick KPI targets (copyable)
- Interactive default: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 350ms, error < 0.5%
- High-sensitivity: P95 < 200ms, error < 0.25%
- Batch/async: P50 < 1.5s, P95 < 3s, error < 1%
- Cost guideline: delta < +30% first 72h vs baseline or escalate to product finance.

Short changelog (working):
- 2025-02-11: Draft created (Marina)
- 2025-02-20: Added queries and canary expansion heuristic (Diego)
- 2025-03-01: Inserted communication templates and post-launch checklist (Priya)

Notes: keep this doc lightweight. Meant to be read in 3–5 minutes by an operator who is about to flip the canary switch. If you want a full step-by-step incident playbook, see linked Confluence PRD.

--end--
